title: Properties of Light

competencies.text: Discuss properties of light waves in communications, navigation, medicine, and entertainment.
Identify innovations such as soundproofing, amplifiers, LEDs, holograms, and lasers.

days.title: What Light Is
days.content:
🎯 Learning Target

This week you will describe the properties of light waves and how they are used in communication, navigation, medicine and entertainment, including innovations such as LEDs, lasers and fiber optics.

💡 Light Is an Electromagnetic Wave

Light is energy that travels as an electromagnetic (EM) wave. It needs no medium — that is how sunlight crosses empty space to reach Earth. In a vacuum it travels at c = 3 × 10⁸ m/s, the fastest speed possible. In water and glass it slows down.

🌊 Wave Properties

PropertyMeaningWhat it changes
Wavelength (λ)Distance from one crest to the nextColor: red ≈ 700 nm, violet ≈ 400 nm
Frequency (f)Waves passing a point each second (Hz)Energy: higher f, more energy
AmplitudeHeight of the waveBrightness

c = f × λ

Because c is fixed, a shorter wavelength means a higher frequency. Violet light has a shorter wavelength and more energy per photon than red light.

✅ Quick Check

3 questions — read each explanation.

scenario.text: Sunlight reaches Earth through empty space, but sound from the Sun never does. Why?

choices.label: Light needs no medium; sound does
Light is louder than sound in space
Sound travels faster than light
Space absorbs all sound frequencies

scenario.explanation: Light is an electromagnetic wave and can cross a vacuum. Sound is a mechanical wave that needs particles to vibrate, so it cannot cross empty space.

scenario.text: Which property of visible light mainly decides its COLOR?

choices.label: Its wavelength
Its amplitude
Its brightness
Its loudness

scenario.explanation: Different wavelengths are seen as different colors (about 700 nm is red, about 400 nm is violet). Amplitude affects brightness, not color.

scenario.text: Blue light has a shorter wavelength than red light. What does this tell you about blue light?

choices.label: It has a higher frequency
It travels faster in a vacuum
It has a lower frequency
It has a larger amplitude

scenario.explanation: With c = f × λ and c fixed, a shorter wavelength means a higher frequency. All colors travel at the same speed in a vacuum.

days.title: Reflection and Refraction
days.content:
🪞 Reflection

When light bounces off a surface, the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection (both measured from the normal, a line perpendicular to the surface).

  • Regular reflection — smooth surfaces like mirrors and calm water form clear images.
  • Diffuse reflection — rough surfaces like paper or walls scatter light; you see the surface, not an image.

Uses: side mirrors, periscopes, road reflectors and the bright strips on school uniforms for night safety.

🔍 Refraction

Light bends when it passes from one material into another because its speed changes. A straw looks broken in water; a swimming pool looks shallower than it is.

  • Convex lenses bring light together — magnifying glasses, cameras, eyeglasses for farsightedness.
  • Concave lenses spread light out — eyeglasses for nearsightedness.
  • Prisms and raindrops refract each color by a different amount, separating white light into a spectrum (rainbow).

🔗 Activity 1 — Match the Pairs

Match each idea to its example. You need 70%; retakes are unlimited.

match.right: Angle of incidence equals angle of reflection
match.why: Both angles are measured from the normal to the surface.

match.right: Clear image in a bathroom mirror
match.why: A smooth surface reflects light in one direction, so an image forms.

match.right: Light scattered by a white wall
match.why: A rough surface reflects light in many directions, so no image forms.

match.right: Straw that looks broken in water
match.why: Light changes speed and direction as it passes from water to air.
It bends light rays together toward a focus.
It spreads light out so the image falls on the retina.
Raindrops refract each color by a different amount.

match.right: Car lights bounced back to the driver
match.why: Reflectors send light back toward its source for night safety.

days.title: The Electromagnetic Spectrum at Work
days.content:
🌈 One Family of Waves

Visible light is a small part of the electromagnetic spectrum. All EM waves travel at c in a vacuum; they differ in wavelength and energy.

Wave (long → short λ)Uses
Radio wavesAM/FM radio, TV, cellular signals, GPS
MicrowavesMicrowave ovens, Wi-Fi, weather radar, satellites
InfraredTV remotes, thermal cameras, night vision
Visible lightSight, photography, fiber-optic internet
UltravioletSterilizing water and tools; causes sunburn
X-raysMedical imaging, airport baggage scanners
Gamma raysCancer radiotherapy, sterilizing medical supplies

Higher-frequency waves (UV, X-rays, gamma) carry enough energy to damage living cells, so exposure must be limited and shielded. Lower-frequency waves (radio, microwaves, infrared) do not ionize cells.

🧭 Navigation and Communication

GPS satellites send radio signals; your phone times them to locate you. Weather radar sends microwaves and reads the echoes from raindrops to track typhoons.

🎯 Activity 2 — Scenario Challenge

Choose the best wave or explanation for each situation. Read every explanation. You need 70%; retakes are unlimited.

scenario.text: Your TV remote still works when you point it at the white wall behind you. Which explanation fits BEST?

choices.label: Its infrared signal reflects off the wall to the TV
Its radio signal passes straight through the wall
Its ultraviolet light is absorbed by the white wall
Its sound waves echo off the wall and reach the TV

scenario.explanation: TV remotes send infrared light. A wall reflects infrared just as it reflects visible light, so the signal bounces to the TV's sensor.

scenario.text: PAGASA tracks a typhoon's rain bands hundreds of kilometers away, at night. Which wave does its weather radar use?

choices.label: Microwaves reflected by raindrops
Visible light from the clouds
Sound waves sent through the air
Gamma rays given off by the storm

scenario.explanation: Doppler weather radar sends microwaves and measures the echoes from raindrops. It works day or night, through clouds.

scenario.text: A hospital must check a patient's fractured leg bone. Which wave is used, and why?

choices.label: X-rays, because bone absorbs them more
Radio waves, because they pass through bone
Infrared, because bone gives off more heat
Visible light, because skin is transparent

scenario.explanation: X-rays pass through soft tissue but are absorbed by dense bone, so bones appear clearly on the image.

scenario.text: A municipality wants to disinfect drinking water without adding chemicals. Which EM wave is suitable?

choices.label: Ultraviolet light shining through the water
Infrared light warming the water a little
Radio waves broadcast across the whole water tank
Visible red light shining on the water

scenario.explanation: UV light carries enough energy to damage the DNA of bacteria and viruses, so UV lamps are used to disinfect water.

scenario.text: A barangay compares two streetlights that give the same brightness: a 20 W LED and a 100 W incandescent bulb. Which conclusion is BEST?

choices.label: The LED changes more of its energy into light
The incandescent gives more light per watt
Both bulbs use the same energy each night
The LED must be five times dimmer than the other

scenario.explanation: Both give the same light, but the LED uses one-fifth of the power. Most of an incandescent bulb's energy becomes heat, not light.

days.title: Light Innovations
days.content:
💡 LEDs

A light-emitting diode produces light when electrons move across a semiconductor. Very little energy becomes heat, so LEDs use about 80–90% less electricity than incandescent bulbs and last many times longer.

🔴 Lasers

A laser gives a narrow, intense beam of one color whose waves stay in step. Uses: barcode scanners at the grocery, eye surgery, cutting metal, laser pointers. Never point a laser at anyone's eyes — the focused beam can burn the retina.

🌐 Fiber Optics

Thin glass fibers carry light signals for internet and phone networks. Light stays inside the fiber by total internal reflection: when it hits the fiber wall at a shallow angle it reflects back in instead of escaping. Fiber carries far more data than copper wire and is not affected by electrical noise.

🖼️ Holograms

A hologram records how laser light reflects from an object from many angles, so the image looks three-dimensional. Holograms on ID cards and banknotes make them hard to fake.

🔐 Formative Check — Escape the Lab

3 lives, 6 keys. You need 70% (5 of 6). Read each explanation.

escape.text: What is the speed of light in a vacuum?
escape.explanation: Light travels about 300,000,000 m/s in a vacuum. 343 m/s is sound in air and 1,480 m/s is sound in water.

escape.text: Which EM wave has the SHORTEST wavelength?

choices.label: Gamma rays
Radio waves
Infrared
Microwaves

escape.explanation: Gamma rays are at the high-frequency, short-wavelength end of the spectrum. Radio waves have the longest wavelengths.

escape.text: Why does light stay inside an optical fiber even when the fiber bends?

choices.label: Total internal reflection at the fiber wall
The glass absorbs light that tries to leave
Gravity pulls the light along the fiber
Light can only travel in a straight line

escape.explanation: When light strikes the inside wall at a shallow angle, it is completely reflected back into the fiber, so it follows the bends.

escape.text: Which statement about lasers is TRUE?

choices.label: They give a narrow beam of a single color
They spread light evenly in all directions
They are made from ordinary sunlight
They are safe to shine into someone's eyes

escape.explanation: Laser light is one color (one wavelength) and stays in a narrow, intense beam — which is also why it can damage the eye.

escape.text: Why are holograms printed on ID cards and peso bills?

choices.label: They are very hard to copy with a printer
They make the card stronger and thicker
They let the card work as a light source
They block X-rays at airport scanners

escape.explanation: A hologram needs laser recording to make, so an ordinary scanner or printer cannot reproduce it. That makes fakes easy to spot.

escape.text: Why do sunglasses with UV protection matter on a bright beach day?

choices.label: UV rays carry enough energy to damage the eye
UV rays make all colors look brighter
UV rays are the light that we see as blue
UV rays only matter during cloudy days

escape.explanation: Ultraviolet light is invisible but energetic; long exposure can damage the cornea and lens. UV-blocking lenses filter it out.
